canonical_statement: For k=10, color every 10-subset of {0,...,19} with one of the 11 colors {0,...,10} so that, for every 11-subset A, the eleven 10-subsets of A receive all eleven colors. The color table is ordered lexicographically as Python itertools.combinations(range(20),10). A successful k=10 construction witnesses the unrestricted existential Erdős problem; rejection or exhaustion at k=10 does not settle other k.
success_criterion: amf.erdos835.k10.v1 checks exactly 184756 table entries and all 167960 eleven-subset constraints and accepts. A no-sorry Lean closure and independent status/fidelity review are still required before a resolution claim.
partial_progress_criterion: Retain certified search-space reductions, symmetry breaking, a reproducible SAT encoding, and independently checkable LRAT evidence excluding k=10; a negative k=10 result is partial progress only.
stop_conditions: A current source establishes or excludes k=10 before the run.
The table ordering or coloring convention cannot be reconstructed independently.
The separately approved experiment budget is exhausted.
